plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with slender silvery-green foliage and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers. Heavily visited by bees and butterflies, it is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June through August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash' because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, bright flower head made up of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark disc of tiny florets that develop into seeds. It thrives in full sun on farms, in gardens, and along roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early fall (July through September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; grown extensively in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, the United States, and France
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day, a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms stay fixed facing east.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with drooping pink-purple petals around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It attracts pollinators and goldfinches and tolerates heat and drought.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer into early fall (June through September)
plants.location: Native to the eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Echinacea's name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone, and Native American peoples used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree with sickle-shaped leaves (phyllodes) and fluffy, fragrant golden ball-like flower clusters. In the Southern Hemisphere, it begins flowering in late winter, with some early blooms appearing in July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July through October)
plants.location: Native to southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.
